 ORDER 1.

These review petitions have been filed under Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC for review of common judgment dated 12/9/2014 passed in 9 RP-88-2022 F.A.Nos.218/2007, 219/2007, 220/2007,
221/2007, 222/2007, 223/2007, 224/2007, 225/2007, 226/2007, 227/2007, 228/2007, 229/2007,
230/2007, 231/2007, 232/2007, 233/2007, 234/2007, 235/2007, 236/2007, 237/2007, 238/2007,
239/2007, 240/2007, 241/2007, 242/2007, 243/2007, 320/2007, 314/2007, 313/2007, 312/2007,
311/2007, 310/2007, 308/2007, 307/2007, 321/2007 and 322/2007, thus the same are being decided by this common order.
2. For the sake of convenience the facts are taken from R.P.No.15/2022.
3. Short facts of the case are that the land of the petitioner was acquired by the State for establishment of Special Economic Zone by issuance of notification dated 3/2/1995 in terms of Varda S/O Manga Thru.

sentences.text:
An award was passed on 14/12/1995 thereby compensation of Rs.1,49,641/- per hectare for unirrigated land and Rs.2,24,461/-
per hectare for irrigated land was granted by the Land Acquisition Officer.

4. The petitioner challenged the award by preferring reference under Section 18 of the Act, which was decided by the learned District Judge vide judgment dated 24/1/2007 thereby enhancing compensation to Rs.2,67,627/- per hectare for unirrigated land and Rs.4,01,404/- per hectare for irrigated land.
5. The petitioner as well as State both challenged the judgment of the District Judge by filing First Appeals.
The said first appeals were as decided by the common judgment dated 12/9/2014 thereby dismissing all the appeal of the land owners as well as State.
6. As such both the bunch of appeals (i.e. appeals by land owners as well as appeals by State) came to be dismissed by this Court by the aforesaid common 10 RP-88-2022 judgment.
7. Against the common judgment dated 12/9/2014 Special Leave Petitions were filed by all the land owners before the Hon'ble Apex Court.
The Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 17/12/2021 dismissed all the SLP's on the ground of delay.
In some of the SLP's the Hon'ble Apex Court mentioned that leave granted, LR's were taken on record but ultimately the SLP's were dismissed on the ground of delay.
The present petitioners contend that this bunch of first appeals were also with respect to the same land acquisition proceedings.

11 RP-88-2022 9. There was yet another bunch of F.A.s i.e First Appeal No. 444/2009 (Shakuntala Bai Vs. State of M.P.) and connected matters (for short the third bunch), this bunch of F.A.s was relates to a Varda S/O Manga Thru.

different (subsequent) land acquisition proceeding around the same area.

10. The second bunch of F.A.s was listed before Lok-Adalat (i.e. F.A. No. 418/2010 etc.), this entire bunch was decided in Lok-Adalat vide award dated 11.02.2017 in terms of the order dated 14.05.2015 passed in the third bunch (i.e.First Appeal No.444/2009 etc.) subject to decision in the SLP (C) No. 20190/2016 pending against the order dated 14.05.2015.
11 . Learned counsel for the petitioners has placed on record the order dated 8/9/2017 passed in SLP (C) No. 20190/2016, deciding the bunch of F.A.No.444/2009.
In the said order all the appeals of the landowners have been dismissed and the appeals preferred by the State are allowed.
As such the amount of compensation has been reduced in that bunch.
However, there is one significant difference in the present matter and the said case.

In the present matter the notification u/S. 4(1) of the Act was issued on 3/2/1995 and the award was passed on 14/12/1995 whereas in the said case of Shakuntala Bai (F.A.No.444/2009), the notification u/S. 4(1) of the Act was published on 3/1/2003 and the award was passed on 27/7/2005.
As such, there is a difference of more than ten years between two proceedings.
As such, the said case is completely different in point of time from the cases included in the present bunch.
There are two different land acquisition proceedings, although around the same area.

As regards the second bunch of F.A.s those were not decided on merits but they were disposed off in Lok-Adalat and that too subsequent to decision in the first bunch of F.A.s vide common judgment dated 12.09.2014.
In fact, the 12 RP-88-2022 judgment passed in the present case was biding on the second bunch of cases but it was not brought to the notice of the Court at the relevant time.
however, an award subsequently passed in Lok-Adalat cannot be ground for review of a judgment delivered on merits.
12. The present review petitions have now been filed by the landowners for claiming benefit in terms of order passed in the case of Shakuntala Bai (supra).

As it has already been pointed out above that the two proceedings are completely different and there is a gap of ten years between the two proceedings this can also not be a ground for review of the order passed by this Court.

13. There is one more aspect, the bunch of first appeals annexed as (Annexure P/4) with this review petition first of all that award was passed in the Lok-Adalat, thus it does not have any preferential value and the second of all the same was made contingent on the outcome of the proceedings in the case of Shakuntala Bai (supra) and in case of Shakuntala Bai (supra) all the SLP's filed by land owners were dismissed by the Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 8/9/2017.
Thus this can also not be a ground to review the judgment passed by this Court on 12/9/2014.
14. Even otherwise also no error apparent is pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner in the impugned judgment.
The one and only ground for review is the orders subsequently passed in the Lok Adalat in a different bunch of first appeals.
Varda S/O Manga Thru.

sentences.text: In view of the above analysis of facts, no case for review is made out.
There is no apparent error on the face of the record of the case.
13 RP-88-2022 16. In R.P.No.14/2022 an additional ground of death of one of the appellant (Meena Devi) has been taken, the date of death of Meena Devi has been mentioned as 13/3/2019.
First of all Meena Devi is not the original appellant.
She was LR of original appellant.
There are other appellants also in the appeal and in any case the date is mentioned as 13/3/2019 whereas the judgment was passed on 12/9/2014.
As such it is not clear that the original appellant expired on which date, no such details were provided and this ground was not raised in SLP before the Hon'ble Apex Court.
Thus it cannot be concluded that on the date of judgment the original appellant was not alive.

17. In R.P.No.42/2022 the date of death is mentioned as 7/9/2020, which has no consequence at all for the simple reason that the judgment was passed well before the death of Bhagwat Singh ie.,
12/9/2014 itself.
18. In R.P.No.102/2022 three persons are reported to have died.
Mukund on 1/9/2016, Jagdish on 29/12/2020 and Chagan on 15/4/2021.
As it can be seen all these persons have died after the pronouncement of the judgment on 12/9/2014 thus this also cannot be a ground for review of the judgment.
19. In R.P.No.103/2022 three persons are reported to have dead ie., Dhulichand who has died on 7/6/2019 and with respect to other two persons Radheyshyam and Parmanand, no dates are provided.
All these persons are legal heirs of Moolchand.
There is no details of death of Moolchand.

Thus in absence of any particulars of date of death, it cannot be concluded that the appellant died before 14 RP-88-2022 the pronouncement of judgment on 12/9/2014.
20.
In R.P.No.86/2022 the date of death of Surendra has been mentioned as 3/11/2016.

However,
Surendra was already on record as legal heir.
Thus it is not clear that the original appellant has died before the pronouncement of the judgment.
Because no details of the same has been provided thus this ground is also not tenable.
In this bunch of petitions, the petitioners have stated that some of the appellants had died before the pronouncement of judgment by the First Appellate Court.
However, neither this fact was pleaded in the SLP's before the Hon'ble Apex Court nor any efforts were made for bringing the LR's on record in the first appeal.
In some of the proceedings before the Apex Court it has come on record that LR's of the deceased are permitted to be brought on record, however, the Hon'ble Apex Court still dismissed the SLP.
It is thus clear that the question stood concluded before the Hon'ble Apex Court.
In view of the order passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in SLP now the present review petitions cannot be entertained.
Varda S/O Manga Thru.

sentences.text: In this bunch of review petitions an additional ground has been taken by the petitioners that before the judgment by this Court, the appellant has already died.

However, there is no mention of date nor even any certificate of death has been enclosed with the review petitions, in absence of which this cannot be concluded that death occurred before the pronouncement of judgment hence in absence of 15 RP-88-2022 particulars this ground is not tenable.
23. Learned counsel for the petitioners have placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of Gurnam Singh V/s. Guruvachan Kaur, 2017 (2) JLJ 166.

entities.text: Gurnam Singh V/s. Guruvachan Kaur, 2017 (2) JLJ 166
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In fact in the said case defendants No.2 and 4 have died.
Thus the LR's of those defendants challenged the legality of the impugned order in that case as the right to sue has devolved upon them and order was passed against the dead person.

The significant fact to be noted is that in the said case it was defendants who have died and against whom the order was passed, in the present case it is the appellant who had died thus if he had died before the pronouncement of judgment then it was the responsibility of the LRs to move appropriate application for bringing their names on record.
24.
Apart from above, learned counsel for the petitioner also placed reliance on the judgment of the Apex Court rendered in the case of Kusum @ Ramkusum V/s. Bihari (2005) Vol.4 MPLJ Pg.1 .

entities.text: Kusum @ Ramkusum V/s. Bihari (2005) Vol.4 MPLJ Pg.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case also defendant as well as appellant have died and the Court in view of the said fact considered that the impugned order passed against the dead person was a nullity.
In the present case the situation is quite different.
Here it is a case of land acquisition in which adjudicating authority passed an order of acquisition and quantifying the compensation vide award dated 14/12/1995.
Against this award reference was filed by the persons interested in terms of Section 18 of the Act.
The learned District Judge vide judgment dated 24/1/2007 enhanced compensation.
This judgment of the District Judge was challenged in the first appeal before this Court by the landowners as well as by the State.
These first appeals have been dismissed by the impugned common order dated 12/9/2014.
Here significant fact is that the petitioners are saying in some of the cases one or two appellants had died.
However first of all there is no clear details of death and second of all it was a 16 RP-88-2022 common order deciding the issue finally.

There is no pleading at all that in those cases where some of the persons have died there was any distinguishing factor, on the contrary it has been pleaded that all the cases are identical, in fact the learned counsel for the petitioners has tried to establish that even the subsequent acquisition proceedings were also identical to the present case.

As such the merits of the case would not change as for rest of the cases where the appellants were alive issue has already attained finality and thus the entire exercise becomes and empty formality as, due to similitude of the case the ratio in one case will govern all cases.

25. There is one more significant fact that here the petitioners have filed the review petitions raising many grounds one of that ground is that the appellants have died, thus order could not have been Varda S/O Manga Thru.

sentences.text: However it has not been stated by the petitioners that what efforts did they make to bring their names on record after the death of their predecessors.
In fact they filed SLP's before the Hon'ble Apex Court and brought their names on record.

The Hon'ble Apex Court after permitting their names to be brought on record dismissed the SLP's on the ground of delay and even on merits as mentioned in some of the cases (for reference SLP Civil Diary No.24048/2021 order dated 11/3/2022).
It is thus very late in the day after dismissal of the SLP's to come back in the review before this Court.
The petitioners being the LR's of original appellants were to take steps to bring their names on record

and if their case is accepted as it is also then only effect of that would be that their appeal would stand abated and in view of the fact that their claims have been rejected by the Hon'ble Apex Court on the ground of delay now there is no scope for explaining delay in the present proceedings for setting aside abatement as they were well aware about the impugned order and raised their claim before the Hon'ble Apex 17 RP-88-2022 Court and only after dismissal of the SLP's have resorted to this remedy of review which is nothing but an abuse of process of law.
26.

sentences.text: While taking this view, we may also point out that even in K. Rajamouli this Court took note of both these judgments and explained the principle of res judicata in the following manner:

"4. Following the decision in Kunhayammed [(2000) 6 SCC 359] we are of the view that the dismissal of the special leave petition against the main judgment of the High Court would not constitute res judicata when a special leave petition is filed against the order passed in the review petition provided the review petition was filed prior to filing of special leave petition against the main judgment of the High Court.

The position would be different where after dismissal of the special leave petition against the main judgment a party files a review petition after a long delay on the ground that the party was prosecuting remedy by way of special leave petition.
In such a situation the filing of review would be an abuse of the process of the law.

We are in agreement with the view taken in Abbai Maligai Partnership Firm [(1998) 7 SCC 386] that if the High Court allows the review petition filed after the special leave petition was dismissed after condoning the delay, it would be treated as an affront to the order of the Supreme Court.
But this is not the case here.

In the present case, the review petition was filed well within time and since the review petition was not being decided by the High Court, the appellant filed the special leave petition against the main judgment of the High Court.
We, therefore, overrule the preliminary objection of the counsel for the respondent and hold that this appeal arising out of special leave petition is maintainable."
(Emphasis supplied)
